en: Points of Controversy:
The Refutation Section, Chapter Nineteen.
The Discourse on the Abandoning of Defilements: Does one abandon defilements in the past? Yes.
Does one cause what has ceased to cease, what has departed to depart, what is exhausted to be exhausted, what has set to set,
and what has utterly passed away to pass away utterly? One should not say so …pe… does one abandon past defilements?
“Yes.
“But is it not the case that the past has ceased?
“Yes.”
If the past has ceased, then indeed it should not be said:
"One abandons past defilements. Is it the case that one abandons past defilements?
“Yes. “But is it not the case that the past does not exist?
“Yes.”
If the past does not exist, then indeed one should not say:
"One abandons defilements in the past.
Does one abandon defilements in the future?

“Yes. [The opponent asks: “Does that which is unborn produce birth; does that which is unarisen cause arising; does that which is unmanifested cause manifestation; does that which has not become apparent cause becoming apparent?
“One should certainly not say so…” [and so on].
Does one abandon future defilements?
Yes. But is it not the case that the future is unborn?
“Yes.
“If that which is future is unborn, then indeed, it should not be said:
‘One abandons defilements in the future.’”
Does one abandon future defilements?
Yes. But is it not the case that the future does not exist?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If the future does not exist, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘One abandons defilements in the future.’”
Does one abandon present defilements? Yes.
Does one who is lustful abandon lust, one who is hateful abandon hatred, one who is deluded abandon delusion, and one who is defiled abandon defilements?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that one abandons lust by means of lust, hatred by means of hatred, delusion by means of delusion, or defilements by means of defilements?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
Lust is associated with consciousness; the Path is associated with consciousness?
Yes. Then do two consciousnesses coexist? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is lust unwholesome and the Path wholesome? Yes.
"Are wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, dark and bright states with their counterparts, present before one?
"One should not say so... [etc.
"...Are wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, dark and bright states with their counterparts, present before one?"
“Yes, [it is so].
“Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, these four things are exceedingly remote’?”
Which four? The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first pair that is very far apart...
[as before] ...Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far removed from the wicked.”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Wholesome and unwholesome [states] …pe… come into manifestation.
It should not be said [that this is so].
“Does one abandon past defilements, does one abandon future defilements, and does one abandon present defilements?”—
Yes. [If so,] is it not the case that there are no defilements being abandoned?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...therefore, one abandons past defilements, one abandons future defilements, and one abandons present defilements.
The Discussion on the Abandoning of Defilements is finished.
